title: Latency cost annotated sparkline portfolio
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft that stitches together lightweight benchmark snapshots intended for console collateral: per-model sparklines, hover-detail lat/ cost pairs, and a short guidance blurb for default knobs. Aim is to produce small artifacts designers/product can embed in the Console: compact latency sparklines next to cost-per-1k-tokens, with a 1-click expand to full table.

Summary (tl;dr):
- Quantized variants (q4_0) reduce cost by ~35–42% vs fp16 for sustained workloads, but add 10–25% p99 latency depending on server shape and short-sequence skew.
- Edge-sized instances (T4/RTX6000-class) show lower p50 for tiny models but higher p95/p99 under bursty concurrency vs core (A100) due to queueing.
- Best console experience: show two sparklines per route: p95-latency trend (30d) and cost-per-1k tokens trend (30d). Hover shows small table with p50/p95/p99 + $/1k tokens.

Benchmark setup (short):
- Date window: Jan 06–08 2028 (spot snapshot runs, synthetic load).
- Hardware types: Core pool (A100-80GB, 1x) labeled "core-1xA100"; Edge pool (NVIDIA T4) labeled "edge-t4-1x".
- Models and builds: redwood-base-1b@v202801, redwood-quant-1b-q4_0@v202801, redwood-tiny-350m@v202801.
- Workloads: interactive chat (mean tokens per request = 120, reply ~60), short-completion probes (16 tokens), and sustained streaming (prefix reuse disabled).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16 concurrent requests. Batch opportunistic allowed up to 32 tokens.
- Cost model: infra-only (GPU runtime hours amortized) + soft delta for kernel throughput (converted to $/1k input+output tokens). Numbers are illustrative (not for billing).

Representative numbers (single table snapshot):
-- shorthand: core=A100, edge=T4, q=quantized (q4_0), fp=fp16 --

Model | Target | HW | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1k toks
----- | ------ | -- | ------- | ------- | ------- | --------
base-1b fp | chat(120) | core | 42 | 98 | 150 | 0.88
base-1b q  | chat(120) | core | 48 | 115 | 185 | 0.55
tiny-350m fp | chat(120) | edge | 34 | 210 | 520 | 0.33
base-1b fp | short(16) | edge | 18 | 65 | 110 | 0.95
base-1b q  | short(16) | edge | 22 | 80 | 140 | 0.59
tiny-350m q | chat(120) | core | 30 | 78 | 120 | 0.21

Notes on table:
- Edge T4 runs show lower p50 for tiny model (single-token kernel fast) but much worse p95/p99 when concurrency spikes due to smaller queueing headroom.
- Quantized variant significantly lowers $/1k tokens but increases p95/p99 on core by ~15–22% in our snapshot, driven by extra kernel deserialization and slightly less optimal attention kernels.

ASCII sparklines (30-day normalized trend example):
(Each sparkline is p95 latency normalized 0–1 for visual density in the console)
- base-1b(fp) p95:  ▁▂▃▃▂▂▃▅▆▅▆▇▆▆▅▃▃▂▁▁▃▅▆▇▇▆▅▃▂▁
- base-1b(q)   p95:  ▁▁▁▁▂▂▂▃▃▃▄▅▅▅▅▂▃▂▁▁▁▂▃▄▅▆▅▄▃▁
- tiny-350m(fp) p95: ▁▂▁▂▁▂▂▂▁▂▃▂▃▂▂▁▁▂▁▁▂▂▂▂▃▃▂▁▁
- cost $/1k (base-1b fp -> q):  ▂▂▃▃▃▄▅▅▆▆▆▆▇▇▇▆▅▅▅▄▃▃▂▁

Interpretation and recommended collateral messaging (short bullets):
- "Quantization reduces unit cost but can raise tail latency; surface both metrics near the model selector."
- "For low-latency interactive routes, prefer core-backed fp16 by default; for throughput/cheaper routes use q4 variants with explicit SLA warning."
- "Show p95 and cost-per-1k tokens in the route list; hide p99 but make available in hover-expanded panel — p99 is noisy and skews layout."
- "Provide an actionable knob: 'Prefer cost-savings' toggle — if enabled, prefer q-variants in routing and show expected p95 increase."

Operational caveats (what to capture next run):
- Need deterministic cold-start baseline: current runs mixed prewarmed and on-demand.
- Real-customer traffic mixes are more spiky; run a day-long trace-replay with real session patterns (see linked INF-4321).
- CPU / I/O contributions: we saw ~10–15 ms jitter attributable to kernel deserialization (profiling trace: GH PR/893).

UX mock text for Console tiny-card (50–70 chars in list):
Title: base-1b (fp16) — p95 98 ms • $0.88 / 1k tokens
Hover-expanded:  p50 42 ms | p95 98 ms | p99 150 ms
               Cost: $0.88 / 1k | Quantized variant: $0.55 / 1k (p95 +17%)
               Recommended: Core (low-latency) • Toggle: Prefer cost-savings

Action items (owners):
- [Maya] produce small figset (svg + JSON) for design with the two sparklines + hover table (due Jan 16).
- [Omar] re-run deterministic cold-start sweep and attach perf traces (INF-4321) (due Jan 18).
- [Liam] add cost attribution delta to billing pipeline (PR #893) and annotate product docs (due Jan 24).

Open questions / discussion points:
- What's acceptable default p95 uplift for quantized models before product blocks them as "cost-risk"? (suggest: 20% p95 over baseline)
- Should cost-savings toggle apply per-route or org-wide? (preference: per-route; product to decide)

Quick references:
- Perf trace PR with kernel flame: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/893
- Ticket: JIRA-INF-4321 (cold-start deterministic sweep)
- Slack conversation: #runtime-benchmarks thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01ABCDEF/p1700000000000

This is intentionally short and annotated — next draft will include longer-run day-replay numbers and a small svg kit for Console embed.
